title: Amazon's White Background Rule: How to Pass Every Time (Without a Studio)
description: Amazon requires pure white product photos. Here's how to meet the RGB 255 standard without a photography studio or Photoshop.

blocks.text: If you've ever had an Amazon listing suppressed for "non-compliant main image," you know the pain. You spent hours on that photo. Amazon killed your listing in 30 seconds.
Here's what Amazon actually wants—and how to hit it every single time using tools you already have.
What Amazon Really Requires
Amazon's main image policy is strict:

items.text: No text, logos, watermarks, or props
No shadows, gradients, or off-white tones

blocks.text: A photographed white surface can still appear gray, yellow, or blue because of lighting, exposure, and camera white balance.
The Camera Lie
Even in a professional studio, cameras rarely capture true 255-white. Sensors interpret light, and there's almost always a slight cast—gray, yellow, or blue.
Which means you have two options:

items.text: Build and calibrate a controlled lighting setup, then finish the image in editing
Shoot against a contrasting, uncluttered surface, then use background removal to create a compliant export

blocks.text: For many small catalogs, the second approach is faster to test and easier to repeat.
The 3-Minute Workflow

items.text: Shoot your product on any background (a white sheet, a table, even carpet)
Remove the original background with one click
Apply a pure white background (RGB 255) from the preset options
Export a high-quality file that meets the current size and format rules for your Amazon category

blocks.text: Before publishing, compare the export against Amazon's current product image requirements.
Common Mistakes That Get Listings Suppressed

items.text: Off-white backgrounds. Cream, ivory, or "warm white" all fail Amazon's automated checks.
Heavy or artificial shadows. Keep the background pure white and verify that the image still follows the current category rules.
Reflections on glossy surfaces. Amazon's AI flags these as "additional objects."
Cropping too tight. Product must fill 85%, not 100%. Leave a small margin.

blocks.text: Why AI Beats Manual Editing

Manual editing offers precise control but can take longer. AI background removal is a useful first pass for jewelry chains, hair, fur, and mesh, although difficult edges may still need manual refinement.
For a larger catalog, test both quality and total review time on a small representative batch before choosing a workflow.
